questions.text: Gennady Golovkin is famous for:
questions.hint: Paragraph 2: "Gennady Golovkin… a middleweight boxing champion."

questions.text: Ilya Ilyin won Olympic gold medals in Beijing and London.
questions.hint: Paragraph 4: "Ilya Ilyin won gold medals at two Olympic Games — Beijing in 2008 and London in 2012."

questions.text: How many inter-university tournaments has Amir represented WKU in?
questions.hint: Paragraph 5: "He has already represented his university in three inter-university tournaments."

questions.text: Amir says he has ___ hard for four years and hasn't given up.
questions.hint: Direct quote from paragraph 5.

questions.text: Dr. Akhmetov believes sport builds:
questions.hint: Paragraph 6: "sport builds character."

questions.text: How long has Rustam swum?
questions.hint: Listening 1, statement 4: "He has swum every week since he was ten years old."

questions.text: Kamila has been doing regular exercise for a long time.
questions.hint: Listening 1, statement 3: she has NOT done regular exercise yet.

questions.text: In listening 2, how long has Gulnaz worked at the sports centre?
questions.hint: Listening 2, statement 2: "She has worked at the sports centre for three years."

questions.text: Amir decided to try:
questions.hint: Listening 2, statement 5: "He has decided to try the morning fitness class starting next Monday."

questions.text: Zhibek has run in two local competitions ___ September.
questions.hint: "Since September" = since + point in time.

questions.text: "for" is used with:
opts: A specific date in the past
questions.hint: "for" answers "how long?" — for three years, for a week.

questions.text: She has trained at WKU ___ 2022.
questions.hint: 2022 = point in time → since.

questions.text: Which tense is used with "last year"?
questions.hint: "last year" = specific past time → Past Simple.

questions.text: "Have you ever…?" is used to ask about:
opts: Life experience at any point in time
questions.correct: Life experience at any point in time
questions.hint: "Have you ever?" = Present Perfect — life experience.

questions.text: She ___ (just finish) her training session.
questions.hint: "Just" + Present Perfect: has just finished.

questions.text: "I have seen him yesterday" is correct.
questions.hint: "yesterday" = specific time → Past Simple: "I saw him yesterday."

questions.text: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: She has won the medal in 2020.
She has won in 2020 the medal.
questions.hint: "in 2020" = specific time → Past Simple.

questions.text: How long have you ___ (know) Zhibek?
questions.hint: How long + have/has + past participle. know → known.

questions.text: "Already" and "yet" are used with:
questions.hint: "already" and "yet" connect past actions to now → Present Perfect.

questions.text: "for" and "since" are only used in questions, not statements.
questions.hint: "for" and "since" are used in both statements and questions with Present Perfect.

questions.text: "Tournament" means:
opts: A single game between two teams
A series of games or matches to find a winner
questions.correct: A series of games or matches to find a winner
questions.hint: "Tournament" = a competition with multiple games to find the champion.

questions.text: "Discipline" in sport means:
questions.hint: "Discipline" = the practice of training yourself consistently and with control.

questions.text: "Resilience" means giving up when things get difficult.
questions.hint: "Resilience" = the opposite — the ability to recover and keep going after difficulty.

questions.text: She is a world ___ in boxing — she has never lost a professional fight.
questions.hint: "Champion" = the person who has won a competition; the best in their field.

questions.text: "Compete" means:
opts: To take part in a contest against others
questions.correct: To take part in a contest against others
questions.hint: "Compete" = to take part in a competition against other people.

questions.text: "Dedication" is:
opts: The feeling of losing a match
Great commitment and loyalty to something
questions.correct: Great commitment and loyalty to something
questions.hint: "Dedication" = being devoted and committed to achieving something.

questions.text: An "athlete" is someone who watches sports on TV.
questions.hint: "Athlete" = someone who trains and competes in sports.

questions.text: "Represent" your university in a tournament means:
opts: To watch your university team play
To play or compete on behalf of your university
To manage the university sports budget
To write about the university sports team
questions.correct: To play or compete on behalf of your university
questions.hint: "Represent" = to act or compete on behalf of a group or institution.

questions.text: "Victory" means:
opts: Success or winning in a contest
questions.correct: Success or winning in a contest
questions.hint: "Victory" = winning a competition or battle.

questions.text: He trains with great ___ — he never misses a session.
questions.hint: "Discipline" = consistent effort and self-control in training.
